title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 596-598): Grothendieck is studying, in the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' that follow La Longue Marche, a profinite group S_0^Π Γ^!_{ρ,σ}. It sits in an extension of a group Ẑ^!_{ρ,σ} by μ (≈ ±1). It is split over two index-2 subgroups Z^{!!} and Z^{!!!}. Elements are triples (u,a,b) with u in (a completion of) Z, a in a normaliser-type group N'_ρ, b in N'_σ, subject to congruences modulo Π or a smaller Π_0. Two sign characters ε_2, ε_3 with values in μ cut out sub-versions: Γ^{!!} is given by ε_3(u)=1, and Γ^{!!!} by ε_2ε_3(u)=1. The question on p. 596 (69) is whether the index-4 subgroups S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!!} and S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!!!} are normal in S_0^Π Γ^!. If they were, the extension would descend to extensions of Z^!/Z^{!!} ≅ ±1 and Z^!/Z^{!!!} ≅ ±1 by μ. Since each subgroup is normal in the corresponding index-2 overgroup, normality in the whole group reduces to normalisation by one element x outside it.

This page, case 1:
- x = (τ, τ', τ) from (70) is an involution, so x u x^{-1} = x u x. It lies in S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!!!} ⊂ S_0^Π Γ^{!!!} but not in S_0^Π Γ^{!!}, since ε_3(τ) = -1.
- Take u = (u,a,b) in S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!!}, i.e. u ≡ a ≡ b (Π_0) and ε_3(u)=1. Conjugation acts componentwise: (τ(u), τ'(a), τ(b)).
- This always lies in S_0^Π Γ'. It lies in the Π_0-version iff τ(u) ≡ τ'(a) ≡ τ(b) (Π_0) (72).
- The congruence τ(u) ≡ τ(b) ≡ τ(a) follows from (71). So (72) reduces to τ'(a) ≡ τ(a) mod Π_0. Here τ' = σ^{-1}τσ-type twist, so this means σ^{-1}τ(a)σ = τ(a), i.e. [σ̇, τ(a)̇] = 1 in Ĝ/Π_0 (73).
- By the earlier criterion (35 bis) this is equivalent to ε_2(τ(a)) = 1, i.e. ε_2(a) = 1, i.e. ε_2(u) = 1 (74), using a ≡ u (Π_0).
- Since ε_2(u) = 1 does not follow from ε_3(u) = 1, S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!!} is not normal in S_0^Π Γ^!.

Case 2 begins: test S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!!!} with x = (u_0,a_0,b_0) in S_0^{Π_0}Γ^! but not in Γ^{!!!}. So ε_3(u_0) = 1, ε_2(u_0) = -1, and u_0 ≡ a_0 ≡ b_0 (Π_0). The next page concludes that this subgroup is not normal either.

Net effect: the hoped-for descent of the μ-extension to the ±1 quotients fails in this naive form.
errors: No substantive error on this page. The argument is a routine normality test and its conclusion (non-normality) is consistent with the conditions used.
Minor: the step 'τ'(a) ≡ τ(a) (Π_0) iff σ^{-1}(τ(a)) = τ(a)' tacitly identifies τ' with the σ-twist of τ and passes to Ĝ/Π_0; this is not justified on the page but relies on earlier definitions.

On the following page (80) the contradiction is stated as 'ε_3(u_0)=1, false by 75 a)'. With (75) as written (ε_3(u_0)=1, ε_2(u_0)=-1) it should read ε_2(u_0)=1, contradicting ε_2(u_0)=-1. This is an ε_2/ε_3 slip, not on this page.

ideas.what: Reducing normality of an index-2-normal subgroup H ⊂ K ⊂ G (with [G:K]=2) to normalisation by a single element x ∈ G∖K, chosen to be an involution so that conjugation is computed componentwise.

Translating the normality obstruction into a commutation condition [σ, τ(a)] = 1 modulo Π_0, and then into a sign character condition ε_2 = 1. This is part of the study of whether a μ-extension of a profinite 'Lego/lacets' group descends to ±1 quotients.
ideas.modern_name: computation inside profinite (Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type) symmetry groups of the loop equations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's unpublished Longue Marche follow-up notes; GT itself is credited to Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara
ideas.where_published: Not in the published Esquisse; La Longue Marche (1981) contains related material but this specific computation is unsure.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine verification within a long computation. It shows that two candidate index-4 subgroups are not normal, which gives a negative answer to a descent question. There is no new construction or connection.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: should read 'x ∈ S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!!!} ⊂ S_0^{Π}Γ^{!!!} [crossed-out material] et x ∉ S_0^{Π}Γ^{!!}'.
'et il faut voir si x normalise S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!!}' — correct.
Under (71): 'u ∈ Ẑ, a ∈ N'_ρ, b ∈ N'_σ' (the hat on Z is visible).
After (72): 'est-il dans S_0^{Π_0}Γ' (il est en tout cas dans S_0^{Π}Γ') i.e. a-t-on'.
(73): 'i.e. [σ̇, τ(a)̇] = 1 dans Ĝ/Π_0', with a margin note 'NB'.
Final line of (75): 'b) u_0 ≡ b_0 ≡ a_0 (Π_0)'. The crossed-out line is 'ε_2(u_0)ε_3(u_0) = 1'.
(74) and its continuation: 'Cette condition n'est pas conséquence de la condition ε_3(u)=1, ce qui montre que S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!!} n'est pas invariant dans S_0^{Π}Γ^!' ('donc que' should be 'ce qui').
